clue.text: Video initially helps an England football manager

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word video

parts.note: helps in the sense of makes possible, enables

explanation.surface: Video replays assist a man who once ran the England football team.
explanation.walkthrough: Terry Venables managed the England national football team from 1994 to 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: Terry Venables is a named example of a former England national team manager.

clue.text: Pirate queen and artist captured by Scottish engineer

indicators.note: captured by means the other pieces are held inside the engineer's name

parts.note: James Watt, the Scottish engineer of steam-engine fame
ER, Elizabeth Regina
RA, a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A buccaneering queen and a painter are taken prisoner by a Scots inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides the riverbank animal, the term is old slang for a thief or pirate working on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated slang for a robber operating on rivers or at sea, hence a seagoing thief.

clue.text: Remember order to return

definitions.meaning: a summons back, as of an ambassador or faulty products

explanation.surface: Bear in mind the instruction to come back.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to remember something and an official summons to come back, as with faulty goods.

clue.text: Visit doctor and say what you think, briefly

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to opine is to state your view

explanation.surface: Pop round to see the GP and give your opinion in a few words.
explanation.definitionFit: To call in on someone casually is a synonym for paying them a visit.

clue.text: Delight head of section (credit control)

parts.note: delight means joy

indicators.note: head of asks for the first letter of the word section

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A happy department chief, with credit control in brackets as their job title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A joystick is the lever used to steer an aircraft or game, a hand control.

clue.text: Powerful number about teenager, gutted

indicators.note: about puts the song around the other letters

parts.note: a number is a song or musical piece

indicators.note: gutted means the insides of teenager are removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A forceful song about an adolescent who is devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a song, not a figure; 'gutted' looks like British slang for upset but means emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong and powerful are direct synonyms describing great force.

clue.text: Most of team gathering at lift

indicators.note: gathering means the shortened team collects the other letters inside it
most of means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a football or cricket team is an eleven

explanation.surface: Most of the squad meet up at a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: A football or cricket side has eleven players, so 'team' gives the number spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something up is to lift it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: A court supporting former partner? Absolutely correct

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the later pieces sit beneath the first

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A court case backing an ex-partner, which is spot on.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise in every detail, with no error at all, is what absolutely correct means.

clue.text: Exhausted now tour rearranged

indicators.note: rearranged signals that the letters of now tour are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Tired out after a tour whose schedule has been changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tired out or exhausted, used of a person who has nothing left.

clue.text: Be careful with timepiece, Italian

parts.note: a watch is a timepiece

explanation.surface: Take care of an Italian's wristwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial warning telling someone to take care or mind out.

clue.text: A feature of Hampton Court floor?

parts.note: Hampton Court Palace near London is famous for its hedge maze

explanation.surface: A query about the floor of a royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor' is a verb, to astonish, not the ground underfoot. Hampton Court is a Tudor palace near London with a famous hedge maze.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to stun them with surprise, a verb sense.

clue.text: A new helpful hint re hors d'oeuvre

parts.note: a tip is a helpful hint
re means concerning, or as to

explanation.surface: A fresh piece of advice about starters.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian starter of cold meats and pickles served before the main meal.

clue.text: This problem-solving method could get one taken in all right

indicators.note: could get one suggests the method itself would turn the following words into something new, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever way of solving problems might leave someone fooled, but all right in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' reads as fooled, but those words with 'all right' are the fodder for the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Solving problems by indirect, creative approaches rather than step-by-step logic is the method meant.

clue.text: Infected having caught cold? One might doubt that

indicators.note: having caught means the cold letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: septic means infected

explanation.surface: Is that wound infected, or just a chill? Someone could be dubious.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubter who questions accepted opinions is a person inclined to doubt.

clue.text: Invade once arch rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilt signals that the letters of once arch are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Attack a former archway that has been reconstructed.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude on someone else's territory or rights is to invade it.

clue.text: Defeat inmate with short question

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prison inmate

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a query is a question

explanation.surface: Beat a prisoner with a curt question.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome or vanquish an opponent is to defeat them.

clue.text: Become more involved in refurbishment of kitchen

indicators.note: refurbishment means the letters of kitchen are done up in a new order

explanation.surface: Get more deeply engaged in doing up the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: As the plot does, growing more complicated, the sense of 'involved' here.
explanation.definitionFit: When a plot grows more complicated or intricate it is said to deepen in that way.

clue.text: Young mum, irate, needing refreshment

indicators.note: needing refreshment means the letters of mum irate are freshened up into a new order

explanation.surface: A young mother, angry and in need of a cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: Not yet fully grown or developed is what young means here.

clue.text: Choker with brass spike

parts.note: brass neck is British for cheek or nerve, so brass means neck
to lace a drink is to spike it

explanation.surface: A tight collar decorated with a metal spike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choker' is not someone strangling but a tight-fitting piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A choker is a short tight piece of neck jewellery, an example of the item.

clue.text: Part of film score, perhaps minus canticle I'd composed

indicators.note: composed signals that the letters of minus canticle I'd are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A film soundtrack, perhaps missing a hymn I'd written.
explanation.definitionFit: Background music accompanying a play or film, of which a movie score is an example.

clue.text: Legendary Greek winger?

parts.note: not a footballer on the wing, but the mythical youth who flew on wings of feathers and wax

explanation.surface: A famous Greek wide player in football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a footballer; here it is someone with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this son of Daedalus flew too close to the sun on wax wings.

clue.text: Poet's empty study

parts.note: dry as in a well that is empty
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A writer's bare study room.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the seventeenth-century English Poet Laureate, an example of a poet.

clue.text: Song of praise identified by two articles on mass

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the articles are placed above the next piece

parts.note: an and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: A hymn recognised through a couple of newspaper pieces about Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn or song of praise, often a choral piece in church.

clue.text: Satirist's riddle about women

indicators.note: about means the sifting word goes around the other letter

parts.note: to riddle is to sieve or sift

explanation.surface: A satirical writer's puzzle concerning women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' is the verb to sieve, not a puzzle. Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels, is a classic example of a satirist.

clue.text: Theatre award, not the first received by a haggard columnist

indicators.note: received by means the trimmed award goes inside the haggard word

parts.note: haggard means gaunt

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a Tony is an American theatre award

explanation.surface: A tired-looking newspaper writer is handed a theatre prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tony Awards honour Broadway theatre. The columnist meant answers readers' personal problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper writer who answers readers' personal problems in a regular column.

clue.text: Hearing test

definitions.meaning: a court hearing of a case

explanation.surface: An audiology exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a court hearing of a case and an experiment or test.

clue.text: Doubtful pawnbroker, right to ring American

indicators.note: to ring means to encircle the next letter

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker

explanation.surface: A dubious moneylender about to telephone an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my uncle's' was old slang for the pawnshop. 'to ring' looks like phoning; it means circling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclear is open to doubt, so uncertain or doubtful.

clue.text: Unreliable // quote about a Rolls-Royce coming back

indicators.note: coming back means everything built so far is read backwards
about means the quote word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to quote is to cite

explanation.surface: An undependable remark about a Rolls-Royce returning.
explanation.walkthrough: The container makes CITARRE, which 'coming back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means unpredictable and inconsistent, hence not to be relied upon.
